2.

This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
"To grant him regular bail in the Crime No. 136/2022 of Bevoor Police Station,
registered for the offences punishable U/s. 302, 304b, 498A, R/w 149 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 D.P. Act. pending before Prl. District and Session Judge at Koppal."

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
The petitioner was married to deceased as per the rights and customs and at the time of marriage customary articles and cash of Rs.1,00,000/- was given as dowry.

After the deceased joined the matrimonial home, she came across the photograph wherein accused No.11 was found in compromising position with the petitioner herein and when the same was questioned, vague answers were given.
Accused No.11 and petitioner and others hatched a plan to remove his own wife (deceased) so as to have a happy relationship between accused No.11 and petitioner.
In that regard there was an additional demand of dowry and deceased was sent to her parental house at Bengaluru.

On the fateful day petitioner - accused said to have secured the presence of the deceased and brought her on motorcycle and killed her by strangulating and threw her dead body in a canal as per the case of the prosecution and as is found in column No.17 of the charge sheet.
4. The attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of grant of bail was rejected by the trial Court.
Later on, the petitioner is before this Court.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the dead body was found in a canal which is far away from the place of residence of the petitioner and so also where the deceased was last residing in Bengaluru and therefore absolutely there is no nexus between the incident and the petitioner and petitioner has been falsely Sri.

sentences.text: 6. He further contended that the alleged last seen theory witnesses are all concocted by the prosecution at the behest of the complainant and their statements do not make out that petitioner is the person who had taken the deceased on his motorcycle and returned alone.

7. He also pointed out that there is no definite opinion of the doctor with regard to the death as the dead body was found in a canal 5-6 days later from the death of the deceased and the report is inconclusive and the alleged FSL report are all subject matter of evidence and since charge sheet is filed, continuation of petitioner in judicial custody is no longer warranted and sought for grant of bail.

8. Learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail petition by contending that since the death has taken place within 7 years of marriage, the petitioner - accused is bound to explain as to how the deceased died a homicidal death.

9. She also points out that the material available on record especially the FSL report showing fluid collected from the dead body make out that the death of the deceased is homicidal and not suicidal and therefore the prosecution has rightly invoked Sections 302 and 304B of IPC in the incident and taking note of the gravity of the offences alleged against the petitioner herein and
if stand proved,
petitioner is liable for death penalty or life imprisonment and therefore sought for rejection of bail.

10. She also pointed out that since Section 304B offence having been invoked by the prosecution, the prosecution enjoys presumption under Section 113A and 113B of the Indian Evidence Act and therefore the contention urged on behalf of petitioner that he is innocent of the offence alleged against him cannot be countenanced in law and sought for dismissal of petition.
11.

She further points out that prima facie materials in the form of charge sheet contains CCTV footage where the deceased and petitioner are seen on a motorcycle on the date of incident and therefore the petitioner is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
12. Perused the material on record meticulously in view of the rival contentions of the parties.
On such perusal, it is seen that the dead body of the wife of the petitioner was found in a canal.

After noticing the dead body which was identified as wife of the petitioner, the police investigated the matter thoroughly and collected such materials including the statements of last seen witnesses of petitioner and the deceased.

The investigating agency has also collected the CCTV footages in the toll booths in the road where the petitioner has traveled from Bengaluru to the place of incident along with deceased on his motorcycle.
Recovery of the motorcycle and the fact of alleged killing of the wife of the petitioner is shown by the petitioner.

Based upon voluntary statement recorded,
prosecution has collected such evidence as is contemplated under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act.
13. Whether at all the petitioner has taken away the life of the deceased and then threw her into a canal or not cannot be decided by this Court at this stage by holding a mini trial.

sentences.text:
Further, the material collected on behalf of the prosecution in the form of CCTV footage,
recovery under Section 27 of Indian Evidence Act coupled with the statements of the charge sheet witnesses especially CW.55 and CW.56 prima facie makes out that the petitioner was seen in the company of the deceased on the alleged date of incident.

15. As rightly argued on behalf of prosecution that the prosecution enjoys presumption under Section 113A and 113B of Indian Evidence Act cannot be lost sight of while appreciating the grounds urged in a petition seeking grant of bail.

16. On cumulative consideration of the above material on record, without holding a mini trial, this Court is satisfied that the grounds urged are hardly sufficient to entertain the petition for grant of bail by resorting to the special powers vested in this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
17.

Hence, following order:
ORDER Criminal petition is rejected.
However, the observations made by this Court during the course of this order shall not affect the rights of the parties during trial in any manner whatsoever.
The petitioner is at liberty to renew his request with a successive bail petition if there is positive changed circumstance in his case, especially after examination of material witnesses.
